scope.focus: Fusion energy from absolute first principles through nuclear and plasma physics, confinement, reactor engineering, power-plant energy accounting, experimental evidence, computational methods, systems design, and research-frontier literacy.
includes: Atoms, nuclei, isotopes, binding energy, fusion reactions, and quantitative energy bookkeeping
Plasma formation, collisions, charged-particle motion, confinement, heating, transport, equilibrium, stability, and diagnostics
Magnetic-confinement and inertial-confinement approaches, including tokamaks, stellarators, and laser-driven target physics
Tritium breeding and fuel cycles, neutron effects, materials, blankets, heat extraction, magnets, cryogenics, vacuum, maintenance, and safety
Scientific gain, engineering breakeven, net-electric power balance, availability, economics, deployment constraints, and evidence-aware comparison
Computational plasma physics, reactor systems engineering, critical paper reading, reproducible estimates, research design, and frontier refreshes
delegates: General mathematical machinery may later import explicit prerequisites from Linear Algebra or Complex Analysis rather than silently re-teaching advanced mathematics.
General-purpose software-engineering depth may later import explicit prerequisites from C++ or Computer Systems when computational projects require it.
